title: Measure the checkpoint diff bound and the interactive-move grant before building them

story.i_want_to: measure real working-tree diff sizes and what a UserPromptSubmit hook sees, and record both in one measurement doc
story.so_that: the checkpoint bound and the boundary-move grant are chosen from data, as docs/factory/architecture.md section 9 requires, not guessed

rationale: PRD section 9 leaves two release-7 questions open and says each is settled inside the release, by measurement, before anything depends on it: the diff bound a checkpoint carries (R1, section 7 point 4) and whether a UserPromptSubmit hook can tell that Mark typed the move command (R2). Nothing measures either today: the closest bound is the untyped 16 KiB channel-post body (lib/loopctl/coordination/channel_post.ex:97), which the PRD rules out for checkpoints, and claude-config's UserPromptSubmit hooks (hooks/kb-recall-on-prompt.sh:73 reads .prompt and calls loopctl with a 3 s cap at :306) were never asked where a prompt came from. US-52.41 and US-52.45 read this story's numbers and rule.

acceptance_criteria.description: scripts/factory/measure-worktree-diffs.sh <root>... prints one JSON line per git worktree under the roots with path, repo, branch, base, diff_bytes, untracked_bytes and captured_at, where base is the branch's upstream when set and otherwise its merge-base with origin's default branch, and diff_bytes is the byte count of `git diff --binary <base>` streamed into wc -c, untracked non-ignored files included through intent-to-add in a temporary index (GIT_INDEX_FILE pointing at a copy).
The script never changes a measured worktree: the worktree's index file, its working files and its refs are byte-identical before and after a run.
scripts/factory/diff_bound.exs <jsonl>... prints the sample count, p50, p95, p99 and max of diff_bytes and the chosen bound: p99 rounded up to the next 64 KiB, clamped to the range 256 KiB to 4 MiB.

docs/factory/measurements/release-7.md carries one line `bound_bytes: <n>` holding diff_bound.exs's output for the fleet-wide sample, with the machines measured, the sample count, the percentiles and the date.

scripts/factory/probe-user-prompt-submit.sh, run as a UserPromptSubmit hook, appends one JSON line per prompt (session_id, cwd, the prompt's first 200 characters, its byte length, a UTC timestamp) to the log named by PROBE_LOG, prints nothing and exits 0, including when PROBE_LOG is unset or unwritable.

The measurement doc has one row per origin and platform (Linux on minis, macOS on mac-mini) stating whether UserPromptSubmit fired and the prompt's first token, for: a typed `/work-item-move <item> loop`; a message release 4's host daemon delivers into an idle session; a peer's SendMessage; a subagent dispatch; a headless `claude -p` session; and whether the hook reached loopctl with the session's holder credential within 2 s.

The doc carries one line `grant_rule: slash_command` when a typed command was the only origin whose prompt starts with `/work-item-move` on both platforms, else `grant_rule: fleet_dash_only` with the origin that defeated it; a doc check fails when either line is missing or holds another value.

test_cases.name: the measuring script counts a fixture worktree's diff and leaves it untouched (bash test)
preconditions: scripts/factory/tests/measure-worktree-diffs-test.sh builds a bare origin and a worktree with one pushed commit, a 3000-byte tracked edit, a 500-byte untracked file and an ignored file
steps: sha256 the worktree's index, files and `git for-each-ref` output
run the script on the parent directory
expected_results: one line with diff_bytes covering the edit and the untracked file, not the ignored one; every hash unchanged

test_cases.name: a branch with no upstream is measured against its merge-base
preconditions: the fixture worktree on a local-only branch two commits past origin/main
expected_results: base is the merge-base sha and diff_bytes includes the two unpushed commits

test_cases.name: the bound rule on fixed samples
preconditions: three fixture JSONL files: all under 10 KiB; p99 at 300,001 bytes; p99 at 9 MiB

test_cases.name: the probe logs and never blocks
steps: pipe it to the probe with PROBE_LOG set
again with PROBE_LOG pointing into a read-only directory
expected_results: one line logged, empty stdout, exit 0 both times

test_cases.name: the measurement doc carries the bound, every probe row and the rule (doc check)
steps: grep the doc for bound_bytes, the ten probe rows and grant_rule
expected_results: bound_bytes is an integer in range; grant_rule is one of the two values

technical_notes: Where a diff can live today, and why none serves: story_stage_events.data is capped at 8,000 bytes (Stages.max_event_data_bytes/0, lib/loopctl/delivery/stages.ex:201,399); a channel post body at 16,384 (channel_post.ex:97); the runner's dispatch objects at 48,000 (runner_contract.ex:1164). The bound decides US-52.41's column CHECK and its refusal, so it is measured before US-52.41 builds.

Diff shape matches what a checkpoint will carry (US-52.41, US-52.44, US-52.46): `git diff --binary <base>` over a temporary index in which untracked, non-ignored files are added with `git add --intent-to-add`. Base is the pushed head of the branch, so committed-but-unpushed work counts, as it travels with a move.

Run the script on every machine in claude-config's FLEET_MACHINES (hooks/lib/fleet-name.sh) over `~/workspace/*` and over the runner's runs directory (loopctl-runner's kept worktrees, LoopctlRunner.Worktree.status_after/1 'kept', /home/mkreyman/workspace/loopctl-runner/lib/loopctl_runner/worktree.ex:1360; runner/ after release 2). Live worktrees are the handoff points: a session that stops mid-work leaves exactly this state.

Probe origins: the idle-session delivery is release 4's host-daemon duty (provided by release 4, README names table: host daemon). A headless `claude -p` is how loopctl-runner starts sessions (LoopctlRunner.Session, /home/mkreyman/workspace/loopctl-runner/lib/loopctl_runner/session.ex); if it fires the hook, US-52.45 must refuse grants to non-interactive holders, which it does either way.

The probe hook is registered by a temporary entry in the probing machine's settings and removed after the run; it is not shipped. Probe scripts follow the plain-command rule: one script file per job, run as `bash <script>`.

The holder credential the hook presents is the file US-52.28 writes, $HOME/.claude/loopctl-holders/<session_id>.key, matched by the session_id in the hook's stdin JSON; measure the round trip to GET /api/v1/inbox (US-52.24), the read release 4's hooks already make with it.
non_goals: Building checkpoints: US-52.41. Building the grant: US-52.45.
A standing diff-size metric: the bound is re-measured only when a refusal rate says it is wrong (US-52.41 logs each refusal).

failure_modes.partition: n/a: offline scripts run on each machine against local git; no service is called except the probe's one timed request (AC-52.40.6 records whether it fits in 2 s).
failure_modes.state: AC-52.40.4: the measured bound and the grant rule live in one committed doc; nothing is cached on a machine.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.40.2: a run is read-only, so re-running it adds a sample and changes nothing.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.40.1: diff size is streamed into wc -c, so a huge worktree costs time, never memory.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.40.6: the probe runs inside the measured session on each platform; nothing runs elsewhere.

defaults: Bound rule: p99 rounded up to 64 KiB, at least 256 KiB, at most 4 MiB.
Command text measured: `/work-item-move <item> <target>`; US-52.45 builds the same name.
If grant_rule is fleet_dash_only, US-52.45 builds the user-key path alone and its slash-command criteria are not built.
definition_of_done: docs/factory/measurements/release-7.md committed with samples from minis, x1, ryzen, beelink, nuc and mac-mini, bound_bytes and grant_rule.
The probe hook entry is gone from every settings file it was added to (grep settings.json on both probe machines).
